The criterion requires an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1. The evidence includes two records of ECOG 1 performance status dated 2026-03-10 from two different sources, which meets the criterion requirement. Although there is one instance of ECOG 2 performance status dated 2026-03-11, it is after the documented ECOG 1 status and this criterion is typically assessed at baseline. Since the inclusion criterion is met by the documented ECOG 1 statuses, the patient meets this criterion.
The matched fact covers only part of this criterion; its additional requirements are not documented.

The inclusion criterion requires that the cancer be mismatch repair proficient. Mismatch repair proficiency typically corresponds to microsatellite stability (MSS). Evidence index 15 states 'MSI: microsatellite stable (MSS)', indicating the tumor is mismatch repair proficient. Hence, the patient meets this criterion.

The patient must have prior treatment with chemotherapy regimens containing 5-fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan. The evidence shows treatment with FOLFOX (which includes 5-fluorouracil and oxaliplatin) and FOLFIRI (which includes irinotecan), thus meeting the general chemotherapy requirement. However, the criterion adds conditional requirements based on RAS and HER2 status: If RAS wild-type, prior anti-EGFR therapy with cetuximab or panitumumab is required; if RAS wild-type and HER2 positive, prior HER2 targeted therapy is required. The patient's biomarker evidence indicates a KRAS G12C mutation (RAS mutated), not RAS wild-type, so these conditional requirements do not apply. Since the primary required chemotherapy exposures are documented, the criterion is met. However, because we rely on mutation status interpretation and do not explicitly see documentation of prior anti-EGFR or HER2 therapies (not required here due to mutation), the status is MEETS overall with no contradictory evidence. The date comparisons are not needed as there is no time window specified in the criterion.

The exclusion criterion requires presence of uncontrolled concurrent medical illness that would prevent completion of planned therapy. The patient has documented performance statuses of ECOG 1 on 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-10, but also an ECOG 2 on 2026-03-11, which may suggest some clinical deterioration but does not explicitly confirm an uncontrolled medical illness. No explicit documentation of uncontrolled medical illness or comorbidities is present in the evidence. Therefore, it is unknown whether the exclusion applies due to lack of direct evidence of uncontrolled illness.

The criterion requires no available treatment with curative intent. The evidence shows prior treatments (FOLFOX, FOLFIRI) and metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma diagnosis, but does not explicitly address whether any curative treatment options remain available. There is no direct evidence about the availability or offering of any treatment with curative intent for this patient, so the inclusion criterion cannot be confirmed or denied based on the provided data.

The criterion requires evidence of measurable disease per RECIST v1.1. None of the supplied evidence explicitly documents measurable disease or RECIST assessments. Diagnosis of metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma and liver metastases are noted, but this does not necessarily confirm measurable disease per RECIST criteria. Therefore, inclusion cannot be confirmed based on the current evidence.

The evidence contains general clinical and lab data but does not include any documented investigator opinion or explicit evidence of confounding conditions, interfering therapies, or adverse lab abnormalities meeting this criterion. Therefore, without documented treating investigator opinion or specific disqualifying conditions, the status is UNKNOWN.
